title: Prepare a strategy-card secondary with the usual UI
description: While another player resolves a strategy card, a follower can prepare the secondary using the same components the real decision uses: the strategy secondary panel, the technology picker, the planet selection bar with the map, the structure placement bar and the command token panel. They are fed by a client-made stand-in for the engine's question; answering records a private plan on this device instead of sending anything. When the real question opens the plan is validated and either shown picked in the real panel (Review, default) or played in the background without opening the decision (Auto). Synthetic gallery fixtures, not captured engine states.

shots.heading: Waiting: the prepare chip
shots.caption: Another seat is resolving Technology. A small chip names the card and who played it. It only appears for a follower who has not been asked yet and could pay a strategy token; nobody else sees it.

shots.heading: Follow or skip: the real panel
shots.caption: Opened for Politics. The decision is the real strategy secondary panel (card, played by, printed secondary, strategy tokens, Spend / Skip), fed by a stand-in question built from the card in progress and your own tokens. The banner above says 'Preparing: nothing is sent or spent' and offers Save plan and Clear plan.

shots.heading: Technology: the real technology picker
shots.caption: After Follow, the real technology modal with its cost and tech skips. The list is worked out from your own technologies, so the banner says it is approximate until the real question opens (prerequisite skips, faction waivers and discounts are only known then). Picking and confirming records the plan; nothing is submitted.

shots.heading: Saved
shots.caption: The pick is saved at once. The chip now reads Prepared and names the plan; clicking it opens preparation mode again, 'Clear prepared' revokes it.

shots.heading: Diplomacy: planets glow on the map
shots.caption: The real planet selection bar for 'ready which planet'. Your exhausted planets are highlighted on the map exactly as in the real flow.

shots.heading: Diplomacy: pick on the map
shots.caption: Clicking the planet on the map selects it in the bar; Confirm records it (a second planet follows if you have another exhausted one). Nothing is readied.

shots.heading: Construction: placement
shots.caption: The real structure placement bar with the planet picked on the map. The sites are approximate: the engine also checks space dock rules, your supply and unit upgrades, so the real question may offer fewer.

shots.heading: Leadership: purchase and pools
shots.caption: The real command token panel in its buy mode: how many tokens to buy and which pool each goes to. Influence is counted from your ready planets and trade goods; the payment is planned when the real question opens.

shots.heading: Trade: follow or skip, with a warning
shots.caption: Trade can only be prepared as follow or skip. The note says that if the Trade player replenishes you, no secondary is offered to you at all and the plan is dropped.

shots.heading: Review (default): prefilled in the real decision
shots.caption: The real secondary question opened. The prepared answer, validated against the options the engine actually offers, is marked in the real panel and ready to Confirm in one click, or 'Choose myself'.

shots.heading: Needs review
shots.caption: When the prepared answer no longer validates (here no 'yes' is offered), nothing is prefilled or auto-played. The bar says why and offers 'Clear prepared'; the real decision is open for a manual answer.

shots.heading: Auto: decided in the background
shots.caption: In Auto mode with a valid plan the real question does not open at all. Only a non-blocking toast shows what is being played, with a short Cancel window. The decision UI stays closed while the answer is sent.

shots.heading: Auto: Cancel opens the decision
shots.caption: Pressing Cancel releases the decision: the real panel opens so you can answer yourself. The same happens when the plan does not validate, when the send is rejected, after about eight seconds without progress, and after an undo, redo, restore, reload, reconnect or from a second tab.

shots.heading: Auto: invalid plan opens the UI
shots.caption: Auto mode, but the prepared answer no longer validates: the real UI opens at once with 'Needs review' instead of playing anything.

shots.heading: Phone width
shots.caption: On a 390 px wide screen the banner and the real panel stack under the status bar.

notes.title: Client-only.
notes.text: No server, protocol, history or bot change. A prepared answer is never sent anywhere and never binding; the real answer is an ordinary recorded decision. Preparing replaces the submit handler (a plan is recorded, nothing is sent), so the real components behave exactly as they do for the engine's question.

notes.title: Which card is in progress.
notes.text: The public turn status does not name the card, so the client reads the public event log (the action selection's 'played <Card>' detail) and, for a seat holding one card, infers it from the primary's single unexhausted card.

notes.title: What is approximate.
notes.text: Follow/skip, the Diplomacy planet pick and the Leadership panel (as far as influence goes) come from client data. The technology list, the construction sites and the Leadership payment are estimates: the stand-in is shown with an 'approximate until the real question opens' note and the plan is validated against the real options when they arrive.
